plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual plant with a large, coarse stem topped by a showy flower head with golden ray petals surrounding a dark central disc of tiny florets. The heads track the sun during early development. Widely cultivated for seed, oil, and ornament, and native to North America.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America, Europe, Ukraine, Russia, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually a composite of up to 2,000 tiny individual flowers arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray narrow leaves and slender spikes of tiny tubular flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Harvested for essential oils, sachets, and culinary uses.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, peaking July to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, Bulgaria, and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name, English lavender is native to the western Mediterranean; the Romans used it in bathwater, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning to wash.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms spires of bright magenta-pink flowers that open from the bottom up. It is among the first plants to colonize burned or cleared land and carpets mountain meadows and roadsides in late summer.
plants.location: Alaska, Canada, northern United States, Scandinavia, Siberia, and the Rocky Mountains
plants.funFact: Locals say that when the fireweed blooms reach the top of the stalk, summer is nearly over; it also produces a prized honey.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem, a small tree or large shrub with sickle-shaped phyllodes and dense, fluffy, fragrant golden ball-shaped flower clusters that light up the bush during the southern winter and early spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the golden wattle's green and gold colors inspired the country's official sporting colors.
